title: Come, O Thou Universal Good
description: Come, O Thou Universal Good in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 435 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ Desired”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Come, O thou u-ni-ver-sal good! Balm of the woun-ded con-science, come! The hun-gry, dy-ing spi-rit's food; The wea-ry, wan-d'ring pil-grim's home; Ha-ven to take the ship-wrecked in, My ev-er-last-ing rest from sin!

lines: Balm of the wounded conscience, come!
Haven to take the shipwrecked in,
Come, O my comfort and delight!
My strength and health, and shield, and sun
My boast, my confidence, and might,
My joy, my glory, and my crown;
My tree of life, my paradise.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
